title: Bhagavad Gita — Nishkam Karma (कर्मयोग)
description: Short on acting without attachment to results. Chapter 2, Verse 47.

scenes.narration: श्रीमद्भगवद्गीता का एक अमर संदेश — कर्म का रहस्य।
scenes.image_prompt: Lord Krishna and Arjuna on a chariot at the battlefield of Kurukshetra at dawn, two white horses, epic sky

scenes.sanskrit: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन। मा कर्मफलहेतुर्भूर्मा ते सङ्गोऽस्त्वकर्मणि॥
scenes.transliteration: karmaṇy-evādhikāras te mā phaleṣu kadācana; mā karma-phala-hetur bhūr mā te saṅgo 'stv akarmaṇi
scenes.translation: You have a right to perform your prescribed duty, but you are not entitled to the fruits of your actions.
scenes.narration: कर्मण्येवाधिकारस्ते मा फलेषु कदाचन। तेरा अधिकार केवल कर्म पर है, फल पर कभी नहीं।
scenes.image_prompt: a calm farmer sowing seeds in a golden field at sunrise, serene expression, symbolic of selfless action

scenes.translation: Never consider yourself the cause of the results, nor be attached to inaction.
scenes.narration: फल की चिंता छोड़, निष्काम भाव से अपना कर्तव्य निभा। यही है कर्मयोग।
scenes.image_prompt: a meditating figure glowing with inner peace, lotus, soft divine light, letting go of worldly desires
